en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having one of the most perfectly symmetrical volcanic cone shapes in the world.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the smallest primates in the world and has enormous eyes.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching over 500 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest peak in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a unique lake situated entirely within a volcanic crater on Volcano Island.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features one of the longest navigable underground rivers in the world.
Boracay Island in Aklan is globally renowned for its White Beach, which consists of fine, powdery coral sand.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is a critically endangered species endemic to the tropical forests of the Philippines.
The Verde Island Passage, located between Batangas and Mindoro, is recognized as the center of the world's marine shorefish biodiversity.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected marine sanctuary known for its pristine coral atolls.
